title: Pick the Whole-Vehicle Line
description: Compare three schematic lines, anticipate rear-axle placement, and explain what information a scout must establish before driving.

media.alt: Illustrative rocky red-earth off-road path with a sandstone shelf on the left and an eroded channel on the right.
media.provenance: AI-generated editorial illustration. Not a photograph of a real route, and not evidence of obstacle dimensions, stability or drivability.

scenario.name: The rock shelf and washout
scenario.context: The vehicle is parked safely before a designated trail section. You have an overhead *schematic*, not a surveyed route map. Three apparent routes are marked. None is safe to drive until unknown conditions are verified on foot.
scoutFindings: The left shelf exceeds the fictional example vehicle's verified underbody clearance.
The designated trail corridor includes the middle route and excludes the outer right shoulder.
The washout shoulder is unsupported and must not be used.
After clearing loose stones on foot, the center route has a visible exit and sufficient measured clearance for the fictional example vehicle.

checks.text: Measure the rock shelf and check front, belly and rear clearance
checks.why: The first tire clearing the shelf does not establish differential, belly or rear-axle clearance.

checks.text: Inspect the eroded rut edge for stability and legal trail boundary
checks.why: A smooth shoulder may be unsupported or beyond the designated route.

checks.text: Walk far enough to see all four tire paths and the exit
checks.why: A line should be evaluated across the complete obstacle and exit, not only its entrance.

checks.text: Choose the line based on vehicle body color
checks.why: Exterior color has no bearing on clearance or trail suitability.

checks.text: Assume extra momentum will compensate for missing measurements
checks.why: Momentum cannot make unknown geometry or ground stability safe.

lines.title: A · Climb the shelf
lines.summary: Uses the left rock shelf to avoid loose center stones.
lines.why: The fictional scout findings establish that this shelf exceeds the example vehicle's clearance. Avoid a known underbody contact risk.

lines.title: B · Stay within the verified center
lines.summary: Takes the inspected center route with a confirmed exit and clearance.
lines.why: For this fictional scenario only, the center is the sole candidate with verified clearance, corridor legality and a visible exit. Reassess continuously.

lines.title: C · Use the outer shoulder
lines.summary: Avoids the shelf and rocks by hugging the right edge.
lines.why: The shoulder is unstable and outside the defined trail boundary. Do not widen the trail to avoid an obstacle.

rearQuestion.prompt: Your front tires have cleared the obstacle. What must you assess before proceeding?

options.label: Rear-tire paths, differential and belly clearance, vehicle attitude, and the exit
options.why: A successful front-wheel approach is not proof the remaining vehicle will clear.

options.label: Nothing else—the front tires demonstrate the vehicle will clear
options.why: Rear tires may follow a different path, and the underbody can contact after the front axle passes.

options.label: Add throttle to clear the rear without reassessing
options.why: Unnecessary momentum reduces control and cannot solve unknown rear or underbody clearance.

debrief: Scout the legal route, unstable shoulders and unseen exit before choosing a line.
Evaluate front tires, belly and differential, rear axle and departure—not only the first contact point.
Use vehicle-specific measured clearance rather than estimates from a photograph.
Use a spotter when needed, establish stop signals and a safe escape plan.
Do not widen the trail, bypass closures or drive an unsupported edge. Turning around is a valid choice.
notice: Training schematic only. The overhead line and moving vehicle symbol are conceptual illustrations, not a wheel-path calculation, stability analysis or real-world clearance prediction. Never use this module to authorize an actual obstacle attempt.
